Analysis by Richard Cowan

The National Post is the more conservative of Canada’s two national newspapers (The other is the center/left Globe and Mail.) 

Both would compare favorably with the best in the US, and both have called for the legalization of cannabis, but the Post’s libertarian/conservative editorial pages are generally more to my liking. 

As with most major papers, they print a variety of opinions on their Op-ed page and occasionally even allow government leaders to lie to their readers as a national service. See 

Are The Canadian Tories the Last American Wannabes? Even More Out of Touch With Reality Than Bush. 

Today’s edition has a column by Barbara Kay, one of their regular contributors, “Not your mother's reefer ”. In it Ms Kay urges the NP editors to reverse their position on cannabis prohibition and support state violence against Canadian cannabis users. 

The column raises a number of interesting questions, but not the ones that she intended to raise. Simply, where does the lying start? 

First, let me emphasize that I do NOT think that Ms Kay is deliberately lying. I have never met the lady, but she is actually addressing her editors, and lying to them would be really, really dumb, and other than this piece, I see no evidence that she is that. 

If she were dumb, it would be easy to shrug off this piece. So, the question is rather how does an intelligent person allow herself to get conned into the prohibitionist propaganda regurgitation chain? 

You should click on the link above to read the whole column, which is very literate, even quoting Alexander Pope (“A little learning is a dangerous thing… ”), but let’s just look at the “facts”, ma’am, because Pope was more right than you realized. 

She begins by complaining about “the Post's 2007 editorial on marijuana, enunciated in response to evidence that Canada's marijuana consumption was the highest in the industrialized world: ‘What is really remarkable about Canada's status as a cannabis capital is that if you were to set out looking for reasons to worry about it, you would have an awfully hard time finding them. Legalizing pot makes sense.’” 

What was the editorial board smoking when these words were written? In fact, one Legalizing pot "makes sense" only to those who have a "little learning" on the changed nature of cannabis over the last 25 years.

Obviously, she is totally unfamiliar with the prohibitionist party line, or rather she doesn’t recognize it when she repeats it. Of course, this is the old “marijuana is so much more potent than it used to be back when we thought it was harmless” line, which Morgan and Zimmer traced back to 1974. 

See 

The Iron Law of Prohibition: Potent Pot, New Data and the Old Prohibitionist Party Line and Another Lie. 

and 

Old Lies in A New Package. Drug Czar’s “2008 National Drug Control Strategy” Again Demonstrates the Drug War Is Really A War on Cannabis Users. Part One "Potency" 

One of the great things about Canadian newspapers is that they pay much more attention to news from the UK and Europe, so it should not be surprising that Ms Kay says,“’(S)kunk,’ as Britons call the hybrid form of cannabis in current usage, has offered users a 25-fold increase in tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), cannabis' psychoactive ingredient. The mental and physical effects of this chemical change have been dramatic.” 

Unfortunately, Ms Kay did not try to find out if that was true. 

Here is how Ben Goldacre, the Guardian’s “Bad Science” editor put it on March 24, 2007: Laboratory of the Government Chemist…data on mean potency goes from 1975 to 1989. Resin pootles around between 6% and 10% THC, herbal between 4% and 6%, with no clear trend. The Forensic Science Service data takes over to produce more modern figures, showing not much change in resin, and domestically produced indoor herbal cannabis doubling in strength to between 12% and 14%. 

The rising trend of cannabis potency is gradual, and driven largely by the increased availability of intensively UK grown indoor herbal cannabis. You could argue that intensive indoor cultivation of a plant that is easy to cultivate outdoors is the cannabis industry's reaction to illegality. It is dangerous to import in large amounts, dangerous to be caught growing a field of it. So perhaps it makes more sense to grow it intensively indoors, producing a more concentrated product. There is little incentive to produce a perversely strong skunk product for the mass market, since most people tend not to pay any more for unusually strong skunk. 

There is exceptionally strong cannabis to be found in some parts of the UK market today: but there always has been. The UN Drug Control Programme has detailed vintage data for the UK online. In 1975 the LGC analysed 50 seized samples of herbal cannabis: 10 were from Thailand, with an average potency of 7.8%, the highest 17%. In 1975 they analysed 11 samples of seized resin, six from Morocco, average strength 9%, with a range from 4% to 16%. 

To get their scare figure, the Independent compared the worst cannabis from the past with the best cannabis of today. But you could have cooked the books the same way 30 years ago: in 1975 the weakest herbal cannabis analysed was 0.2%; in 1978 the strongest was 12%. Oh my god: in just three years herbal cannabis has become 60 times stronger. This scare isn't new. In the US, in the mid 1980s, during Reagan's "war on drugs", it was claimed that cannabis was 14 times stronger than in 1970.” 

From 

The Iron Law of Prohibition: Potent Pot, New Data and the Old Prohibitionist Party Line and Another Lie. 

also see, 

European Study Shows Potency of Prohibitionist Propaganda. CBS and The AP Lie to the American People About the Dutch. Surprise! 

and 

500 UK Cannabis Smokers A Week Seek Medical Help In Hospitals Since Downgrading? Or 2 Major UK Papers Lie to Their Readers. Guess Which. 

But it gets worse. Ms Kay goes on to claim: 

“In March 2007, The Lancet, Britain's leading medical journal, declared cannabis to be more dangerous and addictive than LSD and Ecstasy.” 

Someone was trying very hard to deceive Ms Kay. 

I have some serious questions about the methodology used in The Lancet study, but here are the rankings, as described in Medical News Today: 

“In order of overall harm, the 20 drugs were given the following ranking (the most harmful, heroin at number 1 scored nearly 3, while the least harmful khat at number 20 scored less than 1): 

(1) Heroin (most harmful). 

(2) Cocaine. 

(3) Barbiturates. 

(4) Street Methodone. 

(5) Alcohol. 

(6) Ketamine. 

(7) Benzodiazepines. 

(8) Amphetamine. 

(9) Tobacco. 

(10) Buprenorphine. 

(11) Cannabis. 

(12) Solvents. 

(13) 4-MTA (para-methylthioamphetamine). 

(14) LSD. 

(15) Methylphenidate (ritalin).

 

(16) Anabolic steroids.

(17) GHB (gamma hydroxybutyric acid). 

(18) Ecstasy. 

(19) Alkyl nitrites. 

(20) Khat (least harmful). 

The Lancet study authors say, “The fact that the two most widely used legal drugs lie in the upper half of the ranking of harm is surely important information that should be taken into account in public debate on illegal drug use. Discussions based on a formal assessment of harm rather than on prejudice and assumptions might help society to engage in a more rational debate about the relative risks and harms of drugs”. 

Notice that alcohol is ranked at #5, while cannabis is ranked #11. As it happens, The (London) Telegraph reported today, “Cases of alcohol liver disease have trebled to reach 43,548 in 2006/7, mental health disorders due to drinking has more than doubled to 68,005 and the number of people treated for overdosing on alcohol has also doubled to hit more than 27,000 cases… 

A fifth of 11 to 15 year olds drank in the last week drank on average 11.4 units which is the equivalent of four pints of strong lager or four large glasses of wine - the highest ever recorded by the NHS.” 

These numbers provide a useful context for the next claim, which is really not a “fact.” 

“Psychiatry professor Robin Murray of London's Institute of Psychiatry estimates that cannabis usage is causally linked to a full 10% of the U. K.'s 250,000 bipolar patients…” 

Actually, I cannot even find any basis for this “estimate.” Murray has made some truly absurd claims. 

See 

Prophylactic State Violence: The Arrogance and Ignorance of Psychiatric Quackery. Bad Science, Worse Ethics -- Analysis by Richard Cowan 

and 

500 UK Cannabis Smokers A Week Seek Medical Help In Hospitals Since Downgrading? Or 2 Major UK Papers Lie to Their Readers. Guess Which. 

Kay’s prohibitionist propaganda pusher keeps her well supplied with the “latest research”: “Indeed, just this past February, the European Respiratory Journal reported on a New Zealand study indicating that long term cannabis use increases the annual risk of lung cancer in young adults by 8% for every year of use.” 

Indeed, indeed. Not really. 

As NORML Deputy Director Paul Armentano has pointed out, “The results of a recent study from New Zealand reporting a nearly six-fold increased risk of lung cancer for individuals who smoke cannabis are based on only 14 cases, and have never been replicated in large-scale population case-control studies… The widely reported study, published Friday in the European Respiratory Journal, assessed the relative risk of lung cancer associated with marijuana smoking in 79 cases and 324 controls. Of the 79 cases in the study, 70 reported smoking tobacco and 21 smoked cannabis.” 

Moreover, “Previous large-scale population case control studies have also failed to identify a significant cancer risk associated with cannabis consumption. Most recently, a UCLA study of more than 2,200 subjects (1,212 cases and 1,040 controls) reported that marijuana smoking was not positively associated with cancers of the lung or upper aerodigestive tract – even among individuals who reported smoking more than 22,000 joints during their lifetime.”

See 

Annotated NORML Weekly News for February 7, 2008; NORML Responds to “Latest Research”. Cannabinoids Kill Cancer. Noting Obama’s Retreat. 

Next, she swerves off into the absurd: 

“In order to better understand this sea change in experts' opinions and how it applies to Canada, I spoke with Ontario based addiction counsellor and treatment/prevention specialist Don Smyth. As in Britain, Smyth explained, kids here are smoking a hybrid Middle-Eastern/ Asian variety of cannabis that is far more intense and addictive than past varieties….” 

Wow! A “hybrid Middle-Eastern/ Asian variety!” Undoubtedly, it was grown by Osama bin Laden personally. Actually, hybridization is a basic part of all modern botany, but because cannabis is illegal, no one really knows the genealogy of what has been crossed with what. However, it has been done mostly by Americans, Canadians, and Dutchmen.

See 

Front Page Fantasy: The New York Times Pushes Fact Free Journalism Supposedly About “BC Bud” 

“In 1970, pot contained 1% THC. Bud contains 20% THC. Imagine a glass of wine or beer with a similarly proportioned alcohol content and consider the "rush" it would provide.”

See 

Time Magazine Reports BC Bud 20% Less Potent Than Four Years Ago?? Incompetent Prohibitionist Propaganda and Even Worse Journalism. As Some Reporters Die to Find the Truth Others Live to Lie. 

Of course, various types of alcohol are available today that vary in “potency” from 3.5% to 10% for beer, up to 14% for wine, generally from 40% to 60% for spirits, and on up to pure grain alcohol. In other words, you can buy some alcoholic drinks that are more than 20 times as “potent” as the weakest. Also, some of the “weakest” are the most popular, and because they are legal, their potency is clearly marked. 

This seems like a good time to note that Ms Kay began by observing that “Canada's marijuana consumption was the highest in the industrialized world.” 

Yes, that is true, so it must therefore follow that the rate of cannabis use is lower in The Netherlands. In fact, the rate of cannabis use in Holland is less than half the Canadian rate. 

See 

International “Prohibition Situation Report” – DEAland Media Ignore News Showing Cannabis Prohibition Is Counterproductive. Coffee Shop System Survives.

It would seem that anyone sincerely concerned about teen cannabis use would want to copy the Dutch success instead of the American failure. (We are close behind the Canadians.) 

But, no. Instead, she says, “Thus, Smyth and others well-informed on the subject claim it is misleading to identify this super-strength cannabis as a "soft" drug. 

From 1998, See 

Shalala Says That Parents Are Wrong To Be Relieved 

That Their Children Are Using Marijuana Instead Of Heroin! 

Survey Results From California Do Not Support Party Line, So They Are Buried.

 

"Pot or weed essentially no longer exists," Smyth says, grimly concluding, "I am absolutely haunted by the irreparable harms this so-called innocuous drug has brought to the lives of [young users]." 

What a coincidence! I am absolutely haunted by the victims of the state violence supported by Mr. Smyth and Ms Kay. 

See 

Calling All Quacks: The Therapeutic Police State and the Politicization of Medicine. Doctors Cannot Study The Violence of Cannabis Prohibition. Because They Are The Disease, Not The Cure. 

And it is even worse when the victims are also medical patients who need cannabis to live. See 

Prohibitionists to Patients: “Drop Dead!” Police, Politicians, and Quacks Put Cannabis Prohibition Ahead of the Sick, Dying and Disabled. “To Jail In An Ambulance.”

and 

Canadian Court Slaps Health Canada’s Arbitrary Limit On Patient Choice of Growers. Years of Harassing Sick and Dying. Bureaucratic Arrogance. 

But for Ms Kay, not using state violence is “moral indulgence.” 

“British politicians have"drunk large" of the evidence, and reversed their position of moral indulgence. Two weeks ago, the Home Office in the U. K. announced: "Cannabis will be reclassified as a Class B drug, sending a strong message that the drug is harmful." 

It is ironic that she previously referred to “this sea change in experts' opinions”, but if that is so important, why did she not acknowledge that the “British politicians” ignored the “experts’ opinions ” when they reclassified cannabis. 

See 

Fascism on the Right In Italy and On the Left In the UK Brings Bad Cannabis Policies. There Is A Long Tradition Of Ignoring Reports On Cannabis That Don’t Support The Prohibitionist Party Line. 

She concludes, “The verdict on the new marijuana is in, and it's "guilty." I would therefore respectfully ask the Post to reconsider its editorial stance on the legalization of "pot," clearly a superannuated description of cannabis today, and in future commentary on this issue, so critical to our youth's health, exercise a little more intellectual-- ahem-- sobriety.”

I will not sit in judgment, but while a plant cannot be guilty, a human can. We can be guilty of bearing false witness, and "These six [things] doth the LORD hate: yea, seven [are] an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness [that] speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren." 

So perhaps Ms Kay should consider who poisoned her access to the Pierian Spring.

See 

The Seemingly Inexhaustible Torrent Of Prohibitionist Propaganda Reminds Me Of The Greek Myth About Hercules And The Stables Of King Augeas. Analysis By Richard Cowan 

And then follow Pope’s conclusion and not be “too vain to mend.”
